Fictional training material. Prepared 2026-11-09 from the eleven files in our folder.
Documents due to Tannwald: Wed 25 Nov 2026. Remote audit: Thu 10 Dec 2026.
Tannwald's tests: the document is dated on or after 2025-12-10; it names an approver or owner; it is a record, not a description; training reaches at least 95%; incidents are reported within 48 h.

| # | Evidence in draft-pack | Current / owner? | Meets the request? | Main gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | system-list_2026-09.csv (+ vendor page) | Yes: approved 2026-09-02, MD | Partly | Claude Team stores data in the **US**. Clause 7 requires EU/EEA storage unless Tannwald agrees in writing, and we found no such agreement. Free chatbots used until Sept are not listed. |

- Note: Claude was in use 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30 before the rule was approved. Training on "data rules" ran on 3 and 10 Sept, also before approval.

## R4 – Admin access review
- Send: `access-review_2026-08-14.csv` (Servicepult).
- Gaps:
  - No review exists for Sprechband (admin owner: team lead Tannwald desk), Nordlager or Claude Team.
  - adm-03 left 2026-07-31 and was removed 2026-08-14, 14 days later.
  - adm-04 had no MFA until 2026-08-14.
  - Policy rule 2 says quarterly, but there is no earlier review on file. "Checked every quarter" in the IT notes is a description, not a record.
- Action: run and record a review of all four systems before 25 Nov, covering leavers and MFA, approved by the MD. The next quarterly Servicepult review is due about mid-November anyway.

## R5 – Training
- Send: `training-records_2026.csv`.
- Facts: there are 26 rows, but E014 appears twice (2026-09-03 and 2026-09-10). That makes **25 unique staff of 120 = 20.8%**. At least 114 staff are needed for 95%. The only course is "Claude Team intro: data rules".
- Gaps:
  - No data protection training is recorded in the last 12 months. Policy rule 4 requires it every year.
  - The AI training reached only the 25 seat holders. But the AI rule applies to all staff, and the chatbot use happened on the Tannwald desk.
- Action: run data protection and AI-rule training for all staff before 25 Nov (or at least before 10 Dec), and get a new HR export.

## R6 – Incidents with Tannwald data in 2026
- Send: `incident-log_2026.csv`. INC-01 and INC-03 say no customer data, so the full log can go out as it is.
- INC-02:
  - Detected 2026-05-07 09:40.
  - Tannwald told 2026-05-08 16:10, which is **30 h 30 min, within 48 h**.
  - Cause: mail auto-complete.
  - Fix: auto-complete turned off; recipient confirmed deletion.
  - Closed 2026-05-11.
- Check: INC-03 (phishing click). Confirm the affected account had no access to Servicepult or other Tannwald data before we send "none".
- Open: the free chatbot use (see the urgent section above).

## R7 – Restore test
- `backup-report_2026-10.txt` shows that backups run: 31 of 31 jobs in October. It also states that no restore test was done in 2026, against policy rule 3 (twice a year). Sending it alone answers R7 with "no".
- Action: the IT lead runs a restore test now. That means restoring a Servicepult export and a file-share sample from Nordlager, then recording the date, what was restored, the time taken, the result and the approver. Send that record together with the backup report.

## R8 – Information security policy
- `infosec-policy_v3_FINAL.md`: approved 2024-03-12, review due March 2025, so it is **not current**.
- `infosec-policy_v4_DRAFT.md`: not approved. It also says only "Rules 1 to 5 as in version 3", so it is not a complete document.
- Action: write v4 out in full, then have the MD approve and date it before 25 Nov.
- Note: our records show we are not meeting rules 2, 3 and 4 today (quarterly review, restore tests, annual training). Fix the practice; do not weaken the policy wording to pass the audit.

## Not for sending
- `it-notes_2026-10-06.md`: personal, unreviewed notes. Its facts must go into proper records instead (see R3 and R6).
- `infosec-policy_v3_FINAL.md` and `infosec-policy_v4_DRAFT.md`: not current and not approved.

|---|---|---|---|

I've put together a draft evidence pack and an internal review. Nothing has been sent to Tannwald. On the documents we have, only R6 fully meets their request; R1, R2 and R4 are partly met, and R3, R5, R7 and R8 fail.

There is also a bigger problem. The pack, read honestly, shows that we have probably broken clause 7 of the Tannwald contract.

**Urgent: Claude and the free chatbots**
- **Claude Team (since 1 Sep 2026):** our own system list, sub-processor register and AI rule all say Tannwald request text goes into Claude and is stored in the **US**. Clause 7 requires written notice to Tannwald before using AI tools, and EU/EEA storage unless Tannwald agrees in writing. Goran's notes say he found no written notice, and I found no agreement either. The vendor rep's "data stays in Europe" is not in writing and contradicts the vendor page, so we can't rely on it.
- **Free chatbots:** according to Goran's notes, some Tannwald desk agents used free chatbots on their phones until September. If customer data went into them, that is likely a personal data breach. We would then owe Tannwald notice within 48 hours under section 6.2, and we've known since at least 6 October. This needs a decision from the Managing Director, with legal or data protection advice, now rather than on 25 November.
- I would not leave Claude out of the pack. Our own documents name it, so leaving it out would make the pack false. It is better to tell Tannwald first.

**By request**

| # | What we have | Status |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | System list, approved 2 Sep 2026 | Current. Shows US storage for Claude; the free chatbots aren't listed |
| R2 | Sub-processor register, 5 Sep 2026 | The three EU vendors are complete. The Anthropic row has no review date and no legal basis for the US transfer |
| R3 | AI use rule, approved 1 Oct 2026 | Fails: no record of the free chatbot use, no notice to Tannwald, and Claude was used for a month before the rule was approved |
| R4 | Servicepult admin review, 14 Aug 2026 | Covers one of four systems. A leaver was removed 14 days late; one admin had no multi-factor login until the review |
| R5 | HR training export | Fails: 25 of 120 staff trained (20.8%; 95% needed), AI course only, no data protection training at all |
| R6 | Incident log | Meets it: the one Tannwald incident was reported in 30 h 30 min. Still to check: whether the phishing click touched an account with Tannwald data |
| R7 | October backup report | Fails: the report itself says "Restore test: not done in 2026" |
| R8 | Policy v3 (approved Mar 2024) and v4 (unapproved draft) | Fails: v3's review was due March 2025, so it's out of date |

Most gaps can still be closed before the 25 November deadline:
- run and record a restore test
- review admin accounts on all four systems
- train all staff and get a new HR export
- write version 4 of the security policy out in full and get it approved
- fill in the Anthropic row in the register, using only a legal basis we can actually show

The clause 7 breach cannot be closed that way, which is why it needs a decision now.

I tried to re-check the Anthropic vendor page today, but the connection was denied. The printout is from 15 June and says itself to re-read it, so Goran should re-read and reprint it before anything goes out.

Files are in `tannwald-audit-2026/`:
- `INTERNAL_evidence-review.md`: the full review and a 10-point action list with owners. Internal only; don't send it.
- `draft-pack/R1` to `R7`: copies of the documents that could go out. `R8` is empty until version 4 is approved.

# AI use rule, version 1
Fictional training material.
Approved 2026-10-01 by Dragan Ilievski, Managing Director. Owner: Goran Petrovski, IT lead. Valid from 2026-10-01. Next review: 2027-10-01.

Applies to all staff of Vardar Works.
1. The only AI tool for customer data is our Claude Team workspace (25 seats, in use since 2026-09-01). Its data is stored in the US: see vendor-page_claude_2026-06-15.md.
2. Customer data never goes into a personal account or a free chatbot, on a laptop or on a phone.
3. Before you paste a service request, replace the customer's name, address and phone number with [NAME], [ADDRESS] and [PHONE].
4. No passwords, keys or contract files in any chat.
5. Questions go to the IT lead.

The two quoted lines are from the real vendor page. The company and the person who printed it are invented. Fictional training material otherwise.
Source: https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996890
Page date: 15 June 2026. Printed 2026-10-06 by Goran Petrovski, IT lead.

Quoted from the page:
"By default, we may route customer traffic to select countries in the US, Europe, Asia and Australia"
"Note that data is stored in the US."

Vendor pages change. Read the page again before you rely on this.
